card.title: 118th MIXED REGIMENT
card.flavorText: The 118th Mixed Regiment was a unit of the 43rd Division of the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. The division, whose call sign was the Honor Division, was raised in 1943 and assigned to the Central District Army which was responsible for the defense of the Japanese home islands during the Pacific War. However, in 1944 it was assigned to the 31st Army and reorganized into a marine division. That same year the bulk of the division was shipped to Saipan and reached its destination. However, the 118th Regiment, which sailed later, lost two thirds of its men on the way when a US submarine attacked their convoy. In early June 1944 the division had established defensive positions on the island, waiting for imminent invasion by the US forces. On June 15th the Battle of Saipan began and the division suffered significant setbacks against the US forces, losing strategic locations like Hinashita hill. By late June, the division was significantly weakened, and facing defeat, the division commander requested reinforcements or evacuation. With their situation deemed hopeless, the division launched a final, suicidal banzai charge on July 7th, resulting in its complete annihilation. This charge inflicted casualties on US troops but marked the end of the 43rd Division.
